step_matches.reason: Both have the Bureau/Office Chief, designee or manager requesting a purchase card for an employee.
Both have the nominee complete and sign Form A-498.
Both have the nominee complete the GSA web-based purchase card training.
Both have the AO provide written authorization for the purchase.
Both have the cardholder confirm funds are available.
Both have the cardholder complete and attach the Section 508 Determination and Findings form.
The AI has no step for completing other AO-required forms; its S21 covers only ITC approval for IT hardware.
Both have the cardholder make the purchase with the card.
Both have the AO validate receipt of the items and sign the receipt or invoice.
Both result in the accepting employee signing and dating the invoice, though the AI assigns the step to the receiving employee rather than the cardholder.
Both have the cardholder reconcile the monthly SOA; the AI places the signing in a separate step, S30.
Both have the cardholder forward the reconciled SOA to the AO.
Both have the AO review the reconciled SOA; the AI places the signing in a separate step, S33.
Both have the AO forward the SOA to FOC RDG/TOG.
Both have the APC review card usage to find inactive accounts.
Both have the APC provide the inactive account list to each Bureau/Office.
Both have the Bureau/Office confirm the continued need for the inactive account.
Both have the APC suspend the inactive account until confirmation is received.
Both have the APC, auditors or OIG conduct periodic or random reviews of transactions.
Both have the cardholder furnish supporting documentation for the review.
Both have the cardholder review receipts for a questioned charge.
Both have the cardholder contact the merchant to resolve the dispute and document the actions.
Both have the cardholder submit a dispute to the contractor bank.
Both have the AO or Bureau/Office Chief give the APC prior notice of the transfer or separation.
Both have the cardholder provide all records and documentation to the AO.
Both have the cardholder surrender the card to the AO or APC.
Both have the AO note on the final SOA that the departed cardholder could not sign it.
Both have the APC close the cardholder's account.
Both have the Bureau/Office Chief designate a new AO and notify the APC in writing.

decision_matches.reason: The AI merges the Section 508 condition with an IT-hardware condition, and its No branch goes straight to purchase rather than to completing other required forms.
Both test whether another employee accepts or first uses the goods; Yes leads to the invoice signature and No leads to the SOA processing flow.
The AI builds the 3-year inactivity test into step S53 and has no explicit decision for it.
Both test whether the Bureau/Office confirms continued need; Yes leads to confirmation and No leads to suspension.
Both test whether the research confirms a dispute; Yes leads to contacting the merchant and No leads to END.
Both test whether the dispute was resolved with the merchant; Yes leads to END and No leads to the bank dispute.
The condition matches, but the AI's No branch returns to SOA reconciliation instead of closing the account.
